en.askTitle: Change the boxes to your own freelance year and get the same tax plan before your first payment is due
en.runTitle: Austin, Texas: a first-year freelance UX designer on about $95,000 of 2027 income

fields.label: Tax year, filing status, age and state
fields.value: 2027 tax year; single, no dependents; Texas

fields.label: Business costs and separate health premiums
fields.value: About $8,000: laptop, software, a home office corner and health insurance premiums I pay myself

fields.label: Other income or withholding
fields.value: Nobody withholds tax for me now

fields.label: Completed prior-year adjusted tax and AGI
fields.value: 2026 W-2 salary of $88,000; 2026 federal tax fully withheld

en.template: Build a first-year freelance tax plan for {profile}, {income}, {costs}, {other}, and {prior}. Compare penalty protection with a full-tax cash budget. Flag home-office, QBI and retirement eligibility, map payment dates, and explain any assumptions in a calculator. Plan only; do not access accounts, submit returns or make payments.

phases.title: Confirm the 2027 IRS figures, estimated-tax rules, deductions and due dates
phases.note: Safe harbor, uneven income, deductions and payment dates from IRS sources
phases.judgment: It would not treat the $88,000 salary as a prior-year tax figure: “fully withheld” does not mean zero tax, so the calculator asks for the real 2026 tax and AGI. It also put health premiums on a separate line from business costs, because the IRS form instructions treat them differently.

phases.title: Build the guide, an editable calculator and the sourced calculations
phases.note: A practical guide, a calculator you can change, and every calculation traced to a source
phases.judgment: An independent reviewer found a quiet trap: if prior-year AGI was left blank, the calculator would silently pick the 100% safe-harbor rule. The main estimate was unaffected, and the calculator was changed to require both numbers first.

phases.title: Recheck the arithmetic, the calculator and the pages on desktop and phone
phases.judgment: The workbook was recalculated with no errors across 48 formulas and five changed-input tests. 2027 retirement limits that were not yet published are not invented; the retirement sizing is labelled as using 2026 limits.

workers: Checked the IRS rules on safe harbor, uneven income, quarterly due dates and how to pay, and what an $88,000 salary does and does not say about prior-year tax
Checked the IRS rules on health insurance versus business expenses, the QBI deduction, a renter’s home-office corner and retirement-plan limits
Audited the finished guide, calculator and source notes on its own: recomputed the tax, retirement and payment figures and read the workbook’s formulas
